subject: Post-call: BlueOak model-fit checklist & eval next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@blueoakhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BlueOak model-fit checklist & eval next steps

Hi Elena — great to connect today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a focused eval running on Redwood: 

Summary from call:
- BlueOak is evaluating a triage/answer-suggestion flow for clinical intake notes (short to medium contexts, 1-2k tokens typical).
- Primary goals: response accuracy, hallucination risk mitigation, and 95th percentile latency < 300ms for user-facing queries.
- Sensitive data will be processed inside Redwood Dedicated (VPC).

Recommended initial model shortlist (we can iterate after a small benchmark run):
- rw-13b-q4f: best quality/cost balance for safety-sensitive outputs
- rw-7b-intl-q4: lower-cost baseline for throughput testing
- open-mosaic/mpt-7b-instruct (quantized): edge-case behavior comparator

Eval plan (what I propose we run this week):
1) You drop a ~200-sample test set following the attached sample schema (CSV) — redaction already covered in our onboarding checklist.
2) We run a 200-sample run on the three model configs above, produce response output + per-sample model logits and metadata.
3) Scoring: automated precision/recall on labeled gold answers + a manual scorer pass (3 clinical SME annotators) for hallucination/appropriateness. Scoring rubric attached (benchmark_instructions.md).
4) Deliverables: per-model scorecard, latency/cost breakdown, and recommended quantization/profile for production.

Action items / timeline:
- Today: I'll upload the eval harness and prompt bank to the shared drive (see links below).
- EOD Wed: Elena to share sample dataset (blueoak_sample_schema.csv) and a small prompt bank/examples file.
- Fri: Redwood runs the first 200-sample benchmark and shares a preliminary scorecard and per-model logs.

Attachments: blueoak_sample_schema.csv, prompt_set_blueoak_v1.jsonl, benchmark_instructions.md

Shared links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cblueoak and https://redwood.app/evals/BO-4821

Thanks — I'll loop in Marissa (solutions) and Sean (CS) for the scoring setup and SME coordination.

—Kim

Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueOak model-fit checklist & eval next steps

Thanks Kim — concise and helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we prep the sample: 

1) Dataset format: the sample schema looks fine; is JSONL acceptable instead of CSV? Our export pipeline is JSONL-native and includes a few metadata fields (encounter_id, clinician_id_hash, timestamp, input_text, gold_response) — we can drop clinician ids if needed.
2) Scoring: do you provide the manual scorer UI or should we run annotation in-house and share scored files?
3) Data residency: can the Dedicated VPC keep raw notes encrypted at rest and ensure no developer access on Redwood side? Our security team will want to confirm.

Also looping procurement — they asked if there is a short MSA/PO template we can review while the eval runs.

Happy to send a 50-sample JSONL export today if that helps accelerate.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Clinical Innovation, BlueOak Health
elena@blueoakhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueOak model-fit checklist & eval next steps

Hi Elena — quick technical notes on the questions below (copying Kimberly):

1) JSONL vs CSV: JSONL is perfect — the harness ingests a single JSONL with one object per line. Please include the fields you mentioned; we only require input_text and gold_response for the benchmark. The clinician_id_hash is fine to keep for de-dup checks; please ensure it’s a non-reversible hash.

2) Manual scoring: Redwood can host the scorer UI (we use an internal annotation queue for SMEs) and/or accept an annotated JSONL back from you. Given the subject matter, our recommendation is to let your SMEs use our UI for consistency (we will provide per-annotator accounts scoped to the eval). If you prefer in-house scoring, we’ll provide the rubric format and mapping file.

3) Security & residency: Dedicated VPC deployment supports encrypted-at-rest storage (customer KMS). Developer access is blocked by default; we can add an audit log export for your security team to review. I’ll attach a short security note (we will send the SOC2 evidence URL and the Dedicated network diagram in a separate email).

Logistics for the harness run:
- Please upload a 50-sample test file to the shared folder as a start.
- Prompt bank: a small set of 8-12 typical prompts/examples is very helpful for instruction tuning checks (prompt_set_blueoak_v1.jsonl).
- Expected runtime: 200-sample, 3-model run should complete within a business day on dedicated test pool. We will include token-level cost estimates.

On the procurement/MSA question — Kimberly, can you drop the standard eval MSA and a short PO template to procurement?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for the fast answers, Marissa. Looping procurement and confirming next steps: 

- Elena: please upload a 50-sample JSONL to the shared Drive link by EOD today if possible (we’ll use it for a quick smoke run).
- Procurement: attaching the eval MSA and a one-page PO template (see attachments). If procurement needs any redlines for a short-term eval, we can accept a signed PO + SOW for the benchmark window.
- Marissa / Sean: once sample is up I’ll assign the HubSpot deal (BO-4821) to you for run coordination and SME scheduling.

If everyone is aligned I’ll schedule an internal 30-min sync for Thursday to review the first run results.

Thanks — Kim
